subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Ohm's Law: The Master Equation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ohm's Law: The Master Equation usable.

hook.text: One equation rules all simple circuits: V equals I times R.

buildup.text: Voltage is the push, current is the flow, resistance is the opposition.

discovery.text: Double the voltage and current doubles — if resistance stays the same.

twist.text: Georg Ohm published this in 1827 and was ridiculed. Colleagues rejected it.

climax.text: Today every electrical engineer uses Ohm's law daily. It never fails in linear circuits.

punchline.text: V = IR. Three letters, infinite circuits.

quiz.question: According to Ohm's law, what happens if you double the voltage?
options: Current doubles, if resistance stays the same
